patch.value: Brace-ending initializers consume following ASI declarations and members

The ASI recovery guards use expression-ending token sets that omit CloseBraceToken. An object-literal initializer therefore consumes a following semicolon-free export or class field instead of returning control to declaration parsing; the slash lexer heuristic also misclassifies division after an object-literal close.

Object-literal export initializer followed by an export judges both declarations; Object-literal public field followed by another field judges both members; A slash after an object-literal close remains division rather than being rescanned as a regex
Analyze semicolon-free exported variables or public class fields whose initializer ends in an object literal and is followed by another declaration on the next line.
CloseBraceToken is recognized as expression-ending; the next declaration or member is independently judged, while division after an object literal remains division.
CloseBraceToken is absent from the expression-ending set, so recovery consumes the following declaration or member.
Undocumented exports and public fields can bypass the fail-closed documentation gate through an ordinary object-literal initializer.

patch.value: Focused regression passes: two semicolon-free exports are counted separately, a following undocumented public field is reported, and an object-literal division expression remains valid with no false violation.
Added CloseBraceToken to the shared expression-ending classification used by slash rescanning and ASI recovery. Behavioral regressions cover exports, class fields, and division after object literals.
CloseBraceToken now preserves object-literal declaration boundaries and division tokenization.
